title: Demonstrate an understanding of the work-place in the seed industry

lessons.title: How a seed business works
lessons.html:
How a seed business works

A seed company has many parts. Each part does a different job, but they all work together to get good seed to the farmer. When you understand the whole picture, you understand why your own job matters.

The journey of seed

  1. Breeding and research: plant breeders make new cultivars and test them in trials.
  2. Seed production: contract growers plant seed fields. Inspectors check the fields.
  3. Receiving: seed comes to the plant on trucks. It is weighed and sampled.
  4. Processing: machines clean, grade and treat the seed.
  5. Laboratory: analysts test purity, germination and moisture.
  6. Packing and storage: seed is bagged, labelled and stored cool and dry.
  7. Sales and dispatch: seed is sold and sent to co-ops, dealers and farmers.

Support departments

  • Human resources: hiring, pay, leave and training.
  • Finance: paying growers and suppliers, sending invoices.
  • Maintenance: keeping machines and buildings working.
  • Safety, health and environment: keeping people safe.

Who is who

Most workplaces have levels. Workers report to a team leader or supervisor. Supervisors report to a manager. Know who your supervisor is. Go to them first with questions, problems or ideas.

Why your job matters

If the cleaner does not clean the line well, seeds of two cultivars can mix. If a store worker leaves a door open, rain can wet the seed. If a lab analyst makes a mistake, a bad lot can be sold. Every job protects the farmer and the name of the company.

A farmer may only plant once a year. If the seed fails, they cannot simply try again next week. That is why everyone in the seed industry must work carefully.

lessons.title: Rules, rights and responsibilities at work
lessons.html:
Rules, rights and responsibilities at work

Every workplace has rules. Some rules come from the law and some come from the company. Knowing them protects you and your workmates.

Your rights

  • A written contract or letter of employment that says your job, pay and hours.
  • Fair pay, at least the legal minimum wage.
  • Leave, such as annual leave, sick leave and family responsibility leave, as the law and your contract allow.
  • A safe workplace and the right protective clothing for your job (OHS Act 85 of 1993).
  • Fair treatment, with no unfair discrimination.
  • The right to join a trade union.

Your responsibilities

  • Come to work on time and work your hours.
  • Follow instructions and safe work procedures.
  • Wear your PPE: safety boots, dust mask, earplugs, gloves, as your job needs.
  • Look after company equipment and seed.
  • Report accidents, injuries, damage and unsafe conditions at once.
  • Be honest. Never take seed or other company property.

Safety in the seed workplace

HazardWhat to do
Moving machinesNever remove guards; never reach into a running machine
DustWear a dust mask; keep the area clean
Treated seedWear gloves; never eat it; wash hands before eating
ForkliftsStay out of their way; only trained drivers may drive
Heavy bagsBend your knees; get help with heavy loads
NoiseWear hearing protection

Working with others

Treat workmates with respect. Speak to your supervisor if there is a problem. The company has a grievance procedure for complaints you cannot solve yourself. Use it instead of fighting or walking off the job.

Key points

  • Seed moves from breeding to production, processing, testing, packing and sales.
  • Every job protects seed quality and the farmer.
  • You have rights to fair pay, leave, safety and fair treatment.
  • You must follow rules, wear PPE and report problems.
  • Use the grievance procedure for problems you cannot solve.
